title: Apple: Face It, March Is Going to Be Weaker, Says Bernstein - Barron's

https://www.barrons.com/articles/apple-face-it-march-is-going-to-be-weaker-says-bernstein-1516812393 Apple: Face It, March Is Going to Be Weaker, Says Bernstein By Updated Jan. 24, 2018 11:50 a.m. ET Text Size Medium Large 
Remember when Apple ( AAPL ) chief executive Tim Cook said "it's good to question the accuracy of any kind of rumor about build plans,” back in January of 2013? 
He was responding to a question from Bill Shope , then a Goldman analyst, about rumors of cuts in production of iPhone. 
Still, people never stop trying to guess the Apple supply chain. Case in point, amidst mounting rumors of weaker sales of iPhone in the March quarter, Toni Sacconaghi of Bernstein today unleashed a 20-page report scrutinizing the data out recently from 45 suppliers to Apple, and concludes that, yes, March sales of iPhone may be much weaker than currently expected , perhaps 51 million to 57 million units, versus what he believes is consensus for the moment of 62.1 million. 
Sacconaghi, who has an Outperform rating on Apple, offers the message that investors probably should prepare themselves, and not be overly negative. 
Sacconaghi, with help from colleagues David Dai and Mark Li , ran a study of 10 years “of quarterly supply chain and Apple data to determine correlations between Apple's supply chain partners and iPhone revenues." 
He looked at "correlations that were coincident, lagged or led iPhone revenues by 1 and 2 quarters,” and came up with " 10 key component suppliers /ODM/EMS companies that generate (1) at least ~1/4 of their revenue from Apple and (2) have high historical 5-year revenue growth correlation (r-squared > 0.5) with iPhone unit growth." 
Those ten companies are Dialog Semiconductor ( DLG ), Flexium, Catcher, Pegatron, Shenzhen Desay Battery, Hon Hai, Largan, Skyworks, ASE, and Lens Technology. 
The upshot is that Sacconaghi sees a decline in March that is relatively modest in historical terms: "We note that our analysis points to a sequential decline in iPhone units of 33%, which is only modestly higher than the ~30% decline Apple has seen in each of the last 2 years from December to March. 
The bigger question is how investors will respond, and it’s hard to know given good things and bad things: 
We think it is tough to know. On one hand, if iPhone units are 55M (or worse) in March, it would likely point to modest (3% - 4%) iPhone unit growth for full year FY 18, and to a decline in iPhone upgrade rates YoY, despite initial expectations that this would be a super-cycle. On the flip side, (1) myriad supply chain reports have signaled that FY Q2 (March) could be disappointing, and investors are increasingly aware of that possibility; (2) ASP strength could offset much of the weakness and iPhone revenues will likely still grow 15% - 20%+ YoY; (3) an expected lower tax rate is likely to boost EPS estimates; (4) Services and other revenue appears likely to continue to be strong. 
I would note that Dialog Semi shares today are down $1.72, or almost 7%, at $24.06. Its European peer ST Microelectronics ( STM ) is also down $1.39, or almost 6%, at $23.21, and Texas Instruments ( TXN ) is down $8.21, or almost 7%, at $111.68, as its weaker-than-expected outlook last night is being scrutinized today as perhaps affected in part by a slowdown in iPhone.
